---
title: "Export a saved-result HTML report"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Export a saved-result HTML report}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

The report reads already evaluated results. It does not train, select a winning
pipeline, calculate missing metrics or invent confidence intervals. It includes
metric/status tables and performance, calibration and decision curves.

```{r example, eval=FALSE}
library(stormbreaker)
d <- bi_example(120, seed=1)
task <- bi_task(d, "patient_id", "outcome", c("gene_a","gene_b"),
                       decision_thresholds=c(0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5,0.7))
pipeline <- sb_pipeline(learner="logistic")
cv <- run_cv(task,pipeline,folds=3,seed=1)
fit <- fit_final(task,pipeline)
external <- bi_example(100,seed=2)
external$patient_id <- paste0("EXT_",external$patient_id)
prediction <- predict_final(fit,external[c("patient_id","gene_a","gene_b")],
                               id_col="patient_id")
endpoint <- bi_endpoint(external,"patient_id","outcome")
evaluation <- eval_external(prediction,endpoint)
sb_render_report(list(Development=cv, External=evaluation),
                 "my-new-report.html",title="Saved model evaluation")
```

Choose a new filename: both the HTML and companion `<stem>_failures.csv` paths
must be new and are never overwritten. The report is an offline HTML file,
with self-contained SVG images and selectable text
in tables. No Pandoc, external fonts, JavaScript or network requests are needed.
The plotting dependency is the existing optional `ggplot2` package.

Survival sections with a saved prediction horizon or fixed-horizon metric
include `time_auc`, `uno_c`, and `ipcw_brier`, in addition to Harrell C.
The tables and plots retain the saved time target and unit. Different targets
are labeled separately, not pooled or converted; IPCW Brier plots retain
weighted estimates above one. Horizon-free sections do not add these metric
sections, and absent requested values remain unavailable rather than being
computed during report generation.

A single CV result, shared-fold comparison, external evaluation or single-cohort
external comparison is accepted. To include several cohorts, use a uniquely
named list. Each member remains in its own section. Labels do not establish
external independence, and cross-cohort metrics are not pooled. Survival uses
saved Harrell C, with calibration and DCA showing the saved horizon where one
was declared; unrequested curves are not calculated. Default tables and plots
show usable results only, without empty method labels or panels. Issue counts
and a link to the separate failure CSV remain visible. All-failed sections
explicitly say there are no usable results, not that the analysis succeeded.

Patient-level tables, serialized result objects and raw free-text errors are
excluded from the HTML. The separate CSV includes saved pipeline/run/metric
issues with cohort, stage, fold, status and original error text. A pipeline
summary and its detailed issues are separate rows: row count is not a failed
pipeline count. No issues produces a header-only CSV. Review this CSV separately
before sharing or opening in software that interprets formulas in cells.
Cohort/pipeline labels and plotted calibration curves still describe
the source data: review labels and the report before sharing. This is not a
promise of anonymization. Inspect detailed errors in local result objects.
Numbers in tables use eight significant digits; original objects are unchanged.
If an I/O error interrupts the two-file write, a completed CSV can remain;
inspect the paths and choose new filenames rather than overwriting it.

## Whole composite results

Tables, performance/calibration/DCA plots, reports and failure exports accept
whole repeated CV, IECV and stacking CV results. Context columns identify
`repeat_id`, `heldout_cohort_id`, `model_role`, `validation_scheme` and `view_id`.
A `view_id` identifies a structural saved entry, not a patient. Existing
pipeline IDs remain unchanged. Repeated stacks retain member/stack roles.
IECV is method-development validation, not final independent external
validation. No averaging or pooling across repeats or cohorts is performed.

```{r composite-saved-results}
library(stormbreaker)
composite_data <- bi_example(60, seed = 5)
composite_task <- bi_task(
  composite_data, "patient_id", "outcome", "gene_a"
)
composite_result <- sb_compare_repeated_cv(
  composite_task, list(sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic")),
  folds = 3, seeds = c(1, 2)
)
result_table(composite_result, metric = "roc_auc")
sb_failure_table(composite_result)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plot_perf(composite_result, "roc_auc")
}
```

Pass the same whole object to `sb_render_report()` with a new HTML filename;
each saved leaf gets a separate section. Pass a native `sb_run_stack_cv()` or
`sb_run_internal_external_cv()` result in exactly the same way. Stack views
show outer-CV members and the stack, not inner training folds. Failed entries
remain in tables and failure exports; default plots omit unavailable entries.
Different survival horizons and units remain distinct targets.

## Clinician report with model-specific figures

For a saved evaluation `cv`, assemble the core clinical report without
extracting or plotting algorithm-specific technical diagnostics:

```{r clinician-report, eval=FALSE}
views <- clinical_plots(cv)
clinical_report(views, "clinical-summary.html")
```

The report initially expands only the first topic. Expanding every topic does
not compute extra diagnostics. Performance curves retain their saved evaluation
contexts; there is no automatic model-specific figure export.

Only when technical diagnostics are wanted, call the extraction function
explicitly and optionally add the extracted results to a report:

```{r clinician-detail, eval=FALSE}
native <- native_diag(fit, complete = TRUE)
views <- clinical_plots(cv, native = native)
clinical_report(views, "clinical-detail.html", complete = TRUE)
views$status
```

The extractor's `complete` controls which registered diagnostics are requested;
the renderer's `complete` only controls which topics are initially expanded.
Missing captured artifacts remain marked
`missing_capture`; unavailable views retain their reasons. Neither option
reconstructs a missing training history or retrains the model.

Neighbor and other query-specific diagnostics need explicit rows:

```{r clinician-query, eval=FALSE}
native <- native_diag(fit, newdata = query_rows)
views <- clinical_plots(cv, native = native)
```

No training rows are chosen automatically. Query-level figures can expose
individual values; review them before sharing. Individual algorithm extractors
and plotting functions are also available without generating a report.
Saved SHAP and exact-model nomograms can additionally be supplied through
`shap` and `nomogram`; they are not silently computed for every model.

## One figure instead of separate PDFs

Select related available views explicitly, in panel order:

```{r clinician-panel, eval=FALSE}
panel <- plot_panel(views, c("ROC", "Calibration"))
ggplot2::ggsave("discrimination-calibration.pdf", panel, width = 12, height = 5)
attr(panel, "stormbreaker_captions")
```

The caption table retains original titles and explanations outside the image.
Choose a new filename when saving. Panel letters, short titles, axes and legends
remain in the figure. Increase the export size or split complex faceted views
rather than reducing text size. Patchwork is needed only for this combination
step, not for ordinary reports or model fitting.
